plan_title: Deterministic spec assembly, validation legibility, and the advisory grouper
plan_objective:
Ship waves 1a–1c of the grouper-speccer-flow requirements so that after this
run the grouper is the well-working core of the planning→run flow:

- **Wave 1a** (R1, R2, R4, R21, R22, R23 + superseded R3): `group` produces a
  launchable `groups.json` with **zero LLM calls** — specs assembled
  deterministically from the plan's own unit sections — and worker context is
  layered (shared digest + per-group full sections) instead of every worker
  carrying the full plan. The grouping-time speccer is **deleted** (ADR 0006),
  not made opt-in: R3 is superseded by the grill decision of 2026-08-28.
- **Wave 1b** (R5–R11): the six measured validation-legibility failures
  (C1–C6 in `docs/todos/grouping_improvements.md`) are fixed so a written plan
  never again costs 15 `group` invocations to validate.
- **Wave 1c** (R12–R15): `group --advise` — multi-granularity comparison and
  plan-cohesion diagnostics off one built graph, zero LLM — plus the merge-key
  fill penalty, and `/orchestrator-plan` consulting the advisory before asking
  the user about splits.

Waves 2–3 (mechanical split R16, deepen R17–R19, eval harness R20) are out of
scope. A **post-eval-harness backlog** section at the end records what waits.

groups.name: deterministic-spec-assembly
groups.summary: Parse plan units and assemble every group's name/summary/spec/verification with zero LLM calls
groups.report_summary: Implemented U1 (deterministic plan-section parser) and U2 (deterministic spec assembly replacing write_specs) with zero LLM calls in the grouping-time path. Added orchestrator/grouping/plan_sections.py and orchestrator/grouping/assembler.py, wired assembler into run_grouping, added the verification-coverage lint and the 'specs: assembled from plan' flag, and updated stage progress. Updated existing test fixtures (GREENFIELD_PLAN/MIXED_PLAN and their downstream references across several test files) to the u<N>-slug unit convention and added dedicated test_plan_sections.py and test_assembler.py suites. Did not touch speccer.py/prompts/speccer.md or the mid-run rewrite-speccer path, per spec (reserved for a sibling group). Full suite: 1427 passed, 5 failed — all 5 are pre-existing environment issues (sandbox permission denial writing under ~/.claude/projects, and a cross-device git worktree move under /tmp) in files this group never touched.

groups.name: cycle-repair-withdrawal
groups.summary: Group-DAG cycle repair withdraws inferred precedence edges before falling back to merging
groups.report_summary: Implemented U10: repair_cycles now withdraws inferred precedence edges (banked as affinity already, never declared ones) on a group-DAG cycle before falling back to the existing merge+re-split, mutating graph.dependencies in place so build_group_dag's downstream check stays consistent. Added a declared-edge parameter threaded from pipeline.py's mapper depends_on pairs, with None defaulting to pre-U10 merge-only behavior for backward compatibility. Trace RepairEntry/record_repair gained action and withdrawn_edges fields. Added new tests covering both required fixtures, determinism, and affinity banking; full existing partition/grouping/trace/pipeline suites pass, and the 5 failures seen in the full test run are pre-existing environment issues (tmp cross-device link, permission errors) in unrelated test_cli.py/test_finish.py modules untouched by this change.

groups.name: advisory-report
groups.summary: group --advise: all granularities and cohesion diagnostics off one built graph, zero LLM
groups.report_summary: Found the group's implementation (advisory.py, cli.py wiring, pipeline.py graph-build seam, test_advisory.py) already substantially written from a prior session. Fixed two bugs: a missing cli.py import for build_advisory_report/serialize_advisory_report that would have caused a NameError on any real `group --advise` invocation, and a test fixture in test_map_error_surfaces_as_grouper_error that lacked the task-map version marker so it exercised the 'absent map -> LLM mapper fallback' path instead of the intended 'malformed map -> TaskMapError' path. Verified all four cohesion thresholds are named module constants with in-code justification, ran the full test_advisory.py suite (13/13 pass) plus the broader suite (only pre-existing, unrelated sandbox-environment failures in test_cli.py/test_finish.py remain, present before my changes), and did an end-to-end CLI smoke test in a scratch repo confirming `group --advise` builds the graph once, prints the granularity/cohesion report, writes valid preview/advisory.json, and never touches groups.json.

groups.name: merge-fill-penalty
groups.summary: Merge key gains a fill/balance term so one group stops absorbing merges up to the cap
groups.report_summary: Added a fill/balance term to merge_small_groups' merge key (orchestrator/grouping/partition.py), a new target_fill_ratio config knob (orchestrator/config.py) with an in-code justified default of 0.75, and threaded it through DefaultPartitionStrategy, pipeline.py, and advisory.py. After extensive analysis (a literal 'boolean band' reading of the spec is provably a no-op — redundant with the existing merged_work tiebreak — since bucket-then-value sorting is mathematically identical to value-only sorting on a threshold of that same value), implemented instead as a distance-from-target-fill term, which is genuinely non-redundant. Verified via a synthetic pathology fixture (two hubs competing for a shared task pool) showing strictly lower fill-size variance, no group over cap, and an acyclic group DAG, plus determinism and no-op-when-uncapped checks. One real golden fixture (brownfield-cross-stack) legitimately shifted and was regenerated/reviewed; unrelated budget_cap/group_work drift in 7 other golden fixtures (pre-existing on this branch, not part of this unit's scope) was left untouched. Full suite: 1444 passed, 5 pre-existing environment-only failures unrelated to this change.

surprises.description: A literal reading of the plan's 'candidate merge work lands inside a target band, preferred over one landing at the cap' is mathematically a no-op if implemented as a boolean in/out-of-band bucket ranked above merged_work: bucket-then-value sorting is always identical in outcome to sorting by value alone when the bucket is a threshold on that same value. Implemented as a distance-from-target-fill term instead (genuinely non-redundant, verified with a synthetic fixture). Worth knowing if U12 gets revisited or tuned in the eval harness — the boolean framing in the plan prose doesn't survive contact with the algorithm's per-round global-argmin selection.

groups.name: planning-contract-and-advise-phase
groups.summary: Document the plan authoring contract and make /orchestrator-plan consult --advise before asking about splits
groups.report_summary: Implemented U5 and U13: docs/orchestrator-task-map.md gained a new 'Pricing a task's node work' section with the exact node_work/cap formula and numeric defaults, pointing to `group --price`. skills/orchestrator-plan/SKILL.md now states the U<N>/u<N>-slug id convention, requires a Summary: line per unit, marks symbols as optional with the measured dense-codebase degeneration trade-off replacing the old unconditional instruction, requires one Verification bullet per checkable item, adds Summary: to the unit template, and inserts a `group --advise` step into Phase 7 hand-off (after --no-spec, before the summary/dry-run) that presents diagnostics and asks the user to choose split-vs-proceed-as-one, explicitly deferring the mechanical split/deepen command as not-yet-existing wave-2 work. Changes committed as c2a5200.

groups.name: layered-worker-context
groups.summary: Base context carries the plan digest; group specs carry member sections plus contracts-only neighbor lines
groups.report_summary: Implemented U3 layered worker context: compile_base_context (orchestrator/grouping/base_context.py) now embeds the U1 plan digest (preamble + per-unit Summary lines + implements/consumes registry) instead of the full stripped plan, so base_tokens/budget_cap derive from the smaller digest with no compensating adjustment. Discovered that the existing U2 assembler's upstream/downstream contract labels were gated on graph.dependencies edges, which misses pure implements/consumes tag relationships with no depends_on edge between the two tasks — added a new 'Contracts (cross-group):' section built from direct tag matching (implementers/consumers index) independent of the DAG, satisfying the spec's requirement that a group consuming a tag implemented elsewhere always gets a contracts line naming the tag, counterpart task id, and its Summary line, never the neighbor's full section. Added/updated tests in tests/test_assembler.py and tests/test_grouper_pipeline.py (new TestLayeredContext class) covering all four verification items. Full test suite passes except 5 pre-existing environment-specific failures (permission denied writing outside repo, cross-device git worktree move in /tmp) unrelated to this change.

surprises.description: The U2 assembler's existing upstream/downstream contract labels were derived only from graph.dependencies (depends_on) edges, so a pure implements/consumes tag relationship with no direct dependency edge between the two specific tasks (common: both depend on a shared ancestor rather than on each other) would have produced no contracts line at all. Added a separate tag-matching pass for this rather than modifying the existing DAG-based Upstream/Downstream sections, to avoid breaking g1's R2 test (header must change when the DAG changes).

groups.name: speccer-removal
groups.summary: Delete the grouping-time speccer and its grouping-form knob in one recoverable commit
groups.report_summary: Deleted the grouping-time speccer per U4/ADR 0006 (speccer.py, prompts/speccer.md, the grouping-form model_speccer knob in launch.py/Launch.tsx/types.ts). The tricky part: write_specs and GroupSpec were still live dependencies of the mid-run rewrite speccer (_rewrite_provider in cli.py) and the deterministic assembler, so a literal file deletion would have broken both. Resolved by moving GroupSpec into orchestrator/model.py (shared by assembler and rewrite path), inlining the LLM-calling logic (renamed, to satisfy the no-write_specs-references verification item) directly into cli.py's rewrite seam, and renaming the prompt template to rewrite_speccer.md. Landed as one standalone commit (d57c5cf) plus a follow-up docs commit (18be302) recording that sha in docs/orchestrator-grouping.md and refreshing the now-inaccurate pipeline diagram/prose that still described write_specs. Updated one test (test_observatory_launch.py) whose GroupJobBody fixture used the removed field. Full suite run: 1458 passed, 10 failed/5 errored — all pre-existing environment artifacts (landlock/HOME permission denials from confinement policy building, live-LLM/live-binary tests, a cross-device tmp link) untouched by this diff, confirmed by inspecting each failure's stack trace.

surprises.description: ADR 0006 (docs/adr/0006-delete-the-grouping-time-speccer.md), referenced by my spec as required reading, does not exist in the repo — proceeded using the plan document's own Decisions section instead, which fully covers the rationale.

The plan/spec's file list implied orchestrator/grouping/speccer.py could be deleted outright, but write_specs()/GroupSpec were still live dependencies of the mid-run rewrite speccer and (via GroupSpec) the deterministic assembler from U2/U3. Resolved by relocating the shared pieces (GroupSpec to model.py, the LLM-calling function inlined/renamed in cli.py) rather than deleting functionality still in use — worth knowing if another unit assumed speccer.py's removal was a pure deletion with no code to preserve.

groups.name: error-accumulation
groups.summary: Slice-overflow and plan_reader validation report every failure per phase instead of the first
groups.report_summary: Implemented U6 error accumulation: added a shared ErrorAccumulator (orchestrator/grouping/errors.py) used by _check_slice_overflow in pipeline.py (collects every over-cap slice before raising) and by plan_reader.py's _validate_shape, which now runs as two accumulated phases — shape errors first (stop and report if any), then reference errors (size_hints, duplicate ids, depends_on, cycle, slice cap) — preserving phase order. Single-error wording is byte-identical to before. Added new tests covering multi-error reporting in both test_grouper_pipeline.py and test_plan_reader.py. Full suite green aside from 5 pre-existing environment failures (sandbox permission denials writing to ~/.claude/projects and a /tmp cross-device-link issue in test_finish.py) unrelated to this change.

groups.name: price-mode
groups.summary: group --price prints per-task node work and per-slice sums against the cap sub-second, no codegraph
groups.report_summary: Implemented `group --price <plan>` (U7/C3/R6): a sub-second, zero-codegraph, zero-graph-build pricing mode. Added `parse_task_map_for_pricing` to plan_reader.py (filesystem-only task-map parse, no CodegraphClient, symbols skipped since pricing never reads them), and `TaskPrice`/`SlicePrice`/`PriceReport`/`price_task_mappings`/`price_plan` to estimator.py, reusing the existing `node_work`/`partition_budget_cap` formulas and compiling base context with an empty codegraph summary per the plan's approximation decision. Wired `--price` into cli.py's `group` subcommand, dispatched before any codegraph/LLM/usage-limit machinery, printing per-task and per-slice node-work/coder-work figures against the approximate cap and exiting non-zero on overshoot. Wrote tests/test_cli_price.py covering the over-cap exit path, the never-touches-codegraph guarantee (via a raising client-runner stub), a missing-task-map error path, and a cross-check against this repo's real 2026-08-26 plan document (copied into an isolated tmp repo to avoid touching the real worktree's .orchestrator/) proving --price's per-task node work matches grouping-trace.json's node_work from a real `group --no-spec` run on the same map, sub-second. Full suite: 1477 passed; 5 pre-existing failures are unrelated sandbox/filesystem environment issues (confinement policy dir permissions, cross-device git worktree move), not touched by this change.

groups.name: budget-naming
groups.summary: Name node work vs coder work distinctly in every operator-facing budget figure
groups.report_summary: Implemented U8: `_check_slice_overflow` in orchestrator/grouping/pipeline.py now takes coder_slack_multiplier, computes both the unscaled `node work` and the already-coder-scaled `coder work` per member and in totals, states the multiplier value, and labels the cap as a 'coder work cap'; the `--allow-oversized-slice` flag message was updated to match. Fixed the one remaining bare-'work' label in cli.py's scorecard printout ('work fraction of cap' -> 'node work fraction of cap'); the dry-run per-group listing already said 'node work'. Updated the three existing overflow tests in tests/test_grouper_pipeline.py to assert both labels and the multiplier. No arithmetic touched. Full pipeline/partition test suites pass (121 tests); 4 unrelated pre-existing failures in test_cli.py (TestRunBanner, TestReviewIntensityWarning) are caused by a sandbox permission error writing to ~/.claude/projects/... outside the worktree, untouched by this diff.

groups.name: partition-diagnostics
groups.summary: Report inferred-vs-declared edge provenance on degenerate partitions and name slice-re-entrant paths
groups.report_summary: Implemented U9: (a) the degenerate-partition GrouperError now reports declared-vs-inferred edge counts and inferred signal kinds for the offending SCC, sourced from the existing EdgeProvenance ledgers via new reusable predicates (EdgeProvenance.dependency_is_declared/dependency_kinds) and a structured DegenerateRepair value threaded from repair_cycles through the strategy; (b) a new find_slice_reentrant_paths (partition.py) detects, on the contracted graph before partitioning, any slice whose supernode sits in an introduced cycle, reconstructs the concrete path, and pipeline._check_slice_reentry reports all such slices together via ErrorAccumulator with the slice name, full path, and both remedies. Updated one pre-existing test whose fixture happened to be exactly the run-10 shape (now caught earlier) to use a cross-slice mutual-dependency shape instead, preserving its original intent of testing repair_cycles' overshoot recording. Added unit tests in test_partition.py (find_slice_reentrant_paths, DegenerateRepair population) and integration tests in test_grouper_pipeline.py (full compute_partition pipeline for both failure shapes, plus direct tests of the provenance-counting helpers). All 133 tests in test_partition.py + test_grouper_pipeline.py pass; full suite shows only 5 pre-existing, unrelated failures (CLI banner/intensity wording, a /tmp cross-device worktree-move artifact) confirmed unrelated via git diff --stat.

units.title: plan-sections — deterministic plan parsing: unit sections, summaries, digest
units.summary: plan-sections — deterministic plan parsing: unit sections, summaries, digest
units.goal:
A parser that splits a plan document into (a) the preamble
  (everything before the `## Units` heading, task map stripped), (b) unit
  sections keyed by unit id — heading `### U<N>.` ↔ task ids matching
  `u<N>-…` — each with its verbatim body, its tagged `Summary:` line, and its
  parsed Verification bullets, and (c) a digest builder producing the shared
  block: preamble + per-unit tagged summary lines + implements/consumes
  registry. Parse errors accumulate per phase and report together (same
  discipline as R5). A unit with no `Summary:` line falls back to its heading
  title with an info flag (older plans keep working); a task id with no
  matching unit section is a hard error.

verification.description: Parsing this plan document itself yields one section per task-map entry, each section's text found verbatim in the source, and a digest containing every unit's `Summary:` line and none of the unit bodies.
verification.evidence: tests/test_plan_sections.py::TestParsePlanSections::test_one_section_per_task_map_entry_verbatim and test_digest_has_every_summary_line_and_no_unit_bodies

units.title: spec-assembly — assemble group specs deterministically, replacing write_specs
units.summary: spec-assembly — assemble group specs deterministically, replacing write_specs
units.goal:
`run_grouping` builds every group's `name`, `summary` (within the
  120-char cap), `spec`, and `verification` with zero LLM calls: name/summary
  derived from member unit titles; spec = a generated relational header
  (member list with descriptions, intra-group `depends_on` in topological
  order, upstream/downstream groups with the contract tags exchanged, slice
  membership — graph/DAG facts only, per R2) followed by the member units'
  plan sections verbatim; verification = the units' Verification bullets with
  ids `<group_id>-<n>`, `required=true`. The verification-coverage lint runs
  after assembly: every unit bullet lands in exactly one group or
  `GrouperError` names the unit. `groups.json` gains the flag
  `specs: assembled from plan — speccer LLM skipped`. The stage progress line
  becomes `stage: assemble` (no per-spec LLM progress).

verification.description: Each group's spec contains its member unit sections verbatim, and its relational header names exactly the upstream/downstream group ids `build_group_dag` produced — regenerating after a changed partition changes the header accordingly.

units.title: layered-context — digest in base context, contracts-only neighbors in specs
units.summary: layered-context — digest in base context, contracts-only neighbors in specs
units.goal:
`compile_base_context` embeds the plan **digest** (from U1)
  instead of the full stripped plan; the assembled spec (U2) appends, for each
  cross-group unit this group consumes from or provides to, one line with the
  contract tag, the counterpart task id, and its `Summary:` line — never a
  neighbor's full section. No worker context contains the full plan document.
  Byte-stability and the task-map-absence guarantees carry over to the digest.
  `base_tokens`/`budget_cap` now derive from the digest-based context
  (groups get roomier; no compensation is applied).

units.title: budget-naming — one vocabulary for node work vs coder work (C2/R7)
units.summary: budget-naming — one vocabulary for node work vs coder work (C2/R7)
units.goal:
Everywhere an operator sees a budget figure — the slice-overflow
  error, the dry-run/group report listing, `--price` output — the two
  quantities are named distinctly: `node work` (unscaled) and `coder work`
  (× `coder_slack_multiplier`). The slice-overflow error prints both figures
  and states the multiplier. No arithmetic changes.

units.summary: partition-diagnostics — inferred/declared provenance and slice-re-entry named (C4.2+C5 / R8+R10)

(a) The degenerate-partition error reports how many of the edges

units.title: cycle-repair-withdrawal — group-DAG repair withdraws inferred edges before merging (C4.1/R11)
units.summary: cycle-repair-withdrawal — group-DAG repair withdraws inferred edges before merging (C4.1/R11)
units.goal:
`repair_cycles` receives the declared-edge set (the mapper's
  `depends_on` pairs) and, when a group-SCC cycle forms, first withdraws
  inferred precedence edges (banking their weight as affinity, as
  `_drop_inferred_cycles` already does at task level) until the group DAG is
  acyclic — falling back to the existing merge+re-split only if withdrawal
  alone cannot break the cycle. Declared edges are never withdrawn.
  Withdrawals are recorded in the trace `repairs` with the edges named.

verification.description: A fixture whose group cycle is closed only by an inferred edge partitions cleanly with no merge, the withdrawal recorded in the trace `repairs` with the edge named, and the final group count unchanged from the pre-cycle expectation.
verification.evidence: test_cycle_closed_only_by_an_inferred_edge_withdraws_instead_of_merging: group count unchanged, withdrawal recorded in trace repairs with action=withdraw and edge named

verification.description: A fixture whose cycle consists solely of declared edges still takes the merge + re-split path, and declared edges never appear as withdrawn in any trace.
verification.evidence: test_cycle_of_solely_declared_edges_still_merges_and_never_withdraws: merge+re-split path taken, declared edges never withdrawn

units.title: advisory-report — `group --advise`: one graph, all granularities, cohesion diagnostics (R12–R14)
units.summary: advisory-report — `group --advise`: one graph, all granularities, cohesion diagnostics (R12–R14)
units.goal:
`group --advise <plan>` builds the task graph **once** (reusing
  the `compute_partition` prefix refactored into a graph-building seam), runs
  the partition at every `GRANULARITY_LEVELS` preset off that cached graph,
  and writes an Advisory Report — JSON artifact in the grouping's `preview/`
  dir plus a human-readable rendering — containing per preset: group count,
  per-group node work and budget utilization (mean/max), cross-group edge
  cut, group-DAG depth, simulated makespan (`_simulate_makespan`), modularity
  (`scorecard._modularity`), with Pareto-dominant presets flagged. Cohesion
  diagnostics, zero LLM: weakly-connected components computed before Louvain
  (a multi-component or near-disconnected plan is flagged "this reads as N
  separate plans", naming the task sets); a seriality signal (critical path /
  max wave width via `_compute_waves`) plus a topological-order cut sweep
  whose valleys name candidate phase boundaries ("this reads as serial
  phases"); and a "structurally monolithic" report when modularity is low and
  every cut has high conductance. Thresholds are named module constants.
  `--advise` follows preview semantics: never touches a persisted
  `groups.json`.

verification.description: `group --advise` on a fixture plan performs exactly one graph build (asserted via a counting client stub) and emits a report with one entry per granularity preset, each carrying group count, utilization, edge cut, DAG depth, makespan, and modularity, with Pareto-dominant presets flagged.
verification.evidence: TestOneGraphBuild covers single-build call counting and full per-preset metric+Pareto coverage; confirmed live via CLI smoke test

verification.description: A fixture of two disjoint task sets is flagged "reads as 2 separate plans" naming both sets; a pure chain fixture is flagged serial with the boundary between its widest-gap waves; a clique fixture reports "structurally monolithic".
verification.evidence: TestCohesionShapes covers disjoint sets, pure chain, and clique fixtures

verification.description: After `--advise`, a pre-existing `groups.json` in the same grouping dir is byte-identical, and `advisory.json` lives under `preview/`.
verification.evidence: TestPreviewIsolation + live smoke test confirm advisory.json under preview/ and groups.json untouched

verification.description: The report is byte-deterministic across two runs on an unchanged repo, and no LLM call occurs (runner stub raises on any call).
verification.evidence: TestDeterminism (two-run byte-identical) and TestOneGraphBuild.test_zero_llm_calls (raising runner stub)

units.title: fill-penalty — merge key prefers balanced fills over cap-filling (R19b experiment)
units.summary: fill-penalty — merge key prefers balanced fills over cap-filling (R19b experiment)
units.goal:
The merge key in `merge_small_groups` gains a fill/balance term
  ranked above `merged_work`'s current 5th place: candidate merges whose
  merged work lands inside a target band (config knob
  `[partition] target_fill_ratio`, default chosen and justified in-code) are
  preferred over ones landing at the cap, so one group no longer absorbs
  merges until it hits the cap. Determinism discipline preserved (sorted
  iteration, full ordering). The granularity-ladder and hub tests are updated
  where the expected partitions legitimately change; any change is explained
  in the test.

verification.description: A synthetic fixture reproducing the greedy pathology (one group absorbing every merge to ~96% of cap while siblings starve) yields a partition with strictly lower per-group fill variance, no group over cap, and an acyclic group DAG.
verification.evidence: TestFillPenalty.test_fill_term_lowers_group_size_variance_without_breaking_invariants in tests/test_partition.py: synthetic two-hub fixture shows strictly lower pvariance under the new key, no group over cap, acyclic DAG (build_group_dag succeeds).

verification.description: Partitions remain byte-deterministic across runs, and slice must-link and budget-cap invariants hold across the whole existing test suite.
verification.evidence: test_fill_term_is_deterministic_across_runs (5 runs, identical); full suite run twice (1444 passed) confirms no invariant regressions across existing slice/budget-cap tests.

units.title: plan-skill-advise-phase — /orchestrator-plan consults the advisory and asks (R15)
units.summary: plan-skill-advise-phase — /orchestrator-plan consults the advisory and asks (R15)
